title: Connected but Decoupled: Zooplankton Community Structure Across Contrasting Wave Exposure Zones
content:
ABSTRACT

Zooplankton on sandy beaches experience sharp wave-driven hydrodynamic contrasts, but how these forces shape communities given cross-shore connectivity remains unclear. Using Monte Hermoso Beach (SW Atlantic, Argentina 38°59′S, 61°18′W) as a natural experiment, we compared the surf zone and an adjacent shallow subtidal zone with monthly sampling across seven dates (April 2018–April 2019). We quantified abundance, composition, β-diversity, co-occurrence, and copepod functional traits. Communities overlapped strongly and seasonal abundance patterns were synchronized, with moderate inter-zone β-diversity driven mainly by turnover. Yet the surf zone had ~20× higher abundances and contrasting dominance (Acartia tonsa vs. Paracalanus parvus), while within-zone temporal β-diversity was high and co-occurrence was mostly random, indicating stochastic assembly and episodic exchange. Despite taxonomic and numerical decoupling, copepod functional diversity was similar between zones, suggesting connectivity maintains functional redundancy while hydrodynamics regulate local dominance. These results underscore the surf zone as a high-abundance habitat with functional integrity and motivate managing the surf-subtidal interface as a coupled unit under environmental change.
